lesson.title: The Days of the Planets
lesson.subtitle: lunes (Moon), martes (Mars), miércoles (Mercury), jueves (Jove), viernes (Venus), sábado, domingo

hook.title: Why Lunes–Viernes End in '-es'
hook.content: Where did the final -es on lunes, martes, miércoles, jueves, and viernes come from? From the Latin genitive ending -is ('of the Moon, of Mars, of Mercury, of Jove, of Venus')! And because they already end in an unstressed syllable with -s, only sábado (los sábados) and domingo (los domingos) add an -s in the plural!

pattern.title: Esdrújula Accents on Miércoles and Sábado
pattern.content: Remember our Topic 8 rule that third-from-last syllable stress always wears a written accent mark? Look at MIÉR-co-les and SÁ-ba-do!

exercises.prompt: Match each English expression with its Spanish partner:
exercises.target_answer: lunes, martes, miércoles, jueves, viernes, sábado / domingo
exercises.meaning: Monday (Moon), Tuesday (Mars), Wednesday (Mercury, accented!), Thursday (Jupiter), Friday (Venus), Saturday (accented!) / Sunday
exercises.explanation: miércoles and sábado carry esdrújula accents.

exercises.prompt: How do you say 'on Mondays' (every Monday) vs 'on Sundays' (every Sunday)?
exercises.explanation: lunes stays unchanged after los (los lunes); domingo adds -s (los domingos).
Hoy es viernes — naming what day today is uses es without an article.

exercises.idea: say that on Saturday we are going to the movies (al cine)
cues: to the cinema (a + el) → al cine
idea_parts: we are going to the cinema → vamos al cine
exercises.meaning: On Saturday we are going to the movies

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.

summary.outcome: Use all seven weekdays in singular and habitual plural (el lunes / los lunes) and state what day it is with es.

use_example.german: Hoy es jueves y mañana es viernes.
use_example.english: Today is Thursday and tomorrow is Friday.

summary.takeaway: Hoy es lunes ('Today is Monday', no article) vs El lunes voy ('On Monday I go', with el).
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next ([1602] Dates & Appointments): combine numbers, el, and de to express calendar dates.

twist.prompt: Assemble: 'On Tuesday I am going to visit Madrid'
twist.target_answer: El martes voy a visitar Madrid

lunes.etymology_derivation: Spanish uses the masculine article el/los to mean 'on [weekday]': el lunes ('on Monday'), los lunes ('on Mondays')!

martes.context_translation: We'll see each other on Tuesday.

miércoles.etymology_derivation: Mercury's day, with an esdrújula accent.

viernes.etymology_derivation: Venus's day. All five (lunes–viernes) end in -es and stay unchanged in the plural (el lunes / los lunes)!

sábado.context_translation: On Saturday we're going to the movies.

semana.context_translation: This week I have a lot of work.
